new: **تفسیر.** با مجذورِ ولتاژ بالا می‌رود. عددِ [132 kV]{.ltr} با همان $\tan\delta = 0.004$ِ کابلِ فشارِ متوسط حساب شده است؛ برای عایقِ [XLPE]{.ltr}ِ فشارِ قوی مقدارِ رایج حدودِ [0.001]{.ltr} است، یعنی حدودِ [1.1 W/m]{.ltr} (نزدیکِ [7 %]{.ltr} تلفِ رسانا)، و روشِ [IEC 60287-1-1]{.ltr} تلفِ دی‌الکتریکِ [XLPE]{.ltr} را فقط از ولتاژِ فازِ حدودِ [127 kV]{.ltr} به بالا در جریانِ مجاز می‌آورد؛ پس در ولتاژهای بسیار بالا جزءِ محاسبهٔ جریانِ مجاز است
why: The 132 kV case reuses the MV loss tangent 0.004, giving 4.38 W/m and 'nearly a third' of the conductor loss; HV XLPE has tan delta about 0.001 (about 1.1 W/m, ~7 %), and IEC 60287-1-1 only requires XLPE dielectric loss from U0 >= 127 kV, so the claim that it 'enters the rating' at 132 kV is overstated.
evidence: W = 3*omega*C*U0^2*tan(d) = 3*314.2*0.2e-9*76200^2*0.001 = 1.09 W/m vs 14.9 W/m (7.3 %); examples_h.py line 120 hard-codes 0.004 for both cables; IEC 60287-1-1 Table 2 threshold 127 kV for unfilled XLPE (https://jicable.org/TOUT_JICABLE_FIRST_PAGE/2023/2023-E10-4_page1.pdf); 132 kV XLPE example with tan d 0.001 (https://quickfield.com/advanced/cable_dielectric_losses.htm).

why: examples_h.py dielectric(): uses tan(delta)=0.004 for the 132 kV, 1000 mm2 cable (line ~120) and prints 'at 132 kV it is nearly a third'. Use a per-cable tan delta (0.004 for the 33 kV cable as teaching, ~0.001 for HV XLPE), which gives ~1.1 W/m (~7 %), and change the printed line to say the share is small at 132 kV and grows with U0^2 (IEC 60287 counts XLPE dielectric loss from U0 >= 127 kV).

why: With U = I_ch*sqrt(L/C), cable capacitance at the transformer terminals lowers the surge impedance and the chopping overvoltage; a cable-connected transformer does not have a high surge impedance. The real cable issue is multiple re-ignitions with short cables.
evidence: eq-ch24-chop: larger C -> smaller sqrt(L/C) -> smaller U.
